title: intentd spins one core in the store's serve thread, a million syscalls a second in a condvar wait with no timeout, intermittently and without a known trigger
body:
Measured 2026-09-13 on the delivered daemon at e70c3528a (pid 31992, started about 13:58:30Z by `intent daemon restart`), first noticed by dc at 14:07:09Z from `ps` while waiting on a load gate.

What was measured:

- `ps` at 14:07:09Z: 100% CPU, 1:53 CPU time over 8:39 elapsed. Later reads: 2:13 at 14:09:00Z, 2:18 five seconds later, 3:08 at 14:10:16Z, 3:48 at about 14:11:30Z. So the duty cycle was not one flat loop: stretches at 100% and stretches nearer 20 to 70%.
- `top` at about 14:11:30Z: SYSBSD 121,627,650 BSD syscalls cumulative, 113,898 context switches, SYSMACH 18,633. Against 3:48 of CPU that is on the order of a million syscalls a second while hot.
- `ps -M`: one thread carried it all, 2:54 system and 1:23 user at 97.9%, state R; every other thread under a second. By thread order that is the eighteenth thread, which in the `sample` listing is the store's serve thread spawned from `intentd::store::ProjectHandle::open`, not a tokio worker.
- `sample 31992 3`: 2341 samples, every leaf a wait (`__psynch_cvwait` 39795, `mach_msg2_trap` 4791, `__semwait_signal` 4567, `__workq_kernreturn` 2341, `kevent` 2341). The store thread sat 2339 of 2341 in `tokio::runtime::park::Inner::park` under `parking_lot::Condvar::wait_until_internal` reached through `pthread_cond_wait` (no timeout), and 2 samples in `intentd::store::serve` answering `Op::Graphql` for the app's `{threads{id}}` poll. A wait with no timeout that costs a core is returning at once every time: either an unparker signalling a million times a second from a thread that shows no CPU, or the wait returning spuriously.
- The store's `event_log` did not grow across the window, no file under the project tree changed in the two minutes before the read, no client was connected on the web port, the only Unix-socket client was the menubar app's five-second poll, and every git worktree lives under `/private/tmp`, outside the watched tree.
- `intent daemon restart` at about 14:13Z stopped it cleanly ("asked over the wire"). The replacement (pid 58837) read 0.0% at 8s and stayed at 0.0% for the next five minutes (5.9s of CPU in total, the post-start index pass included). So the spin is triggered, not built in.

What is known about the trigger: nothing that survives the evidence. From the CPU time, the onset was about 14:05Z, give or take the duty cycle. In that minute: dc's `cargo build -p intentd` in a detached worktree under an isolated HOME (no path to this daemon); the app polling `intent version`, `daemon status --format json` and `graphql {threads{id}}` every five seconds, as it had since 13:58Z; no commit (the last before the onset was 14:02:51Z, the next 14:13:56Z). The daemon log has no timestamps (0321), so the daemon's own account of the window is two lines.

What is NOT in question: the daemon source is byte-identical between 8a48430ee, the pair dc rehearsed green four times, and e70c3528a; the only library change between them is the `wb show` and `wb pickup` read shape (0322). So this is not a regression of the two items that landed before the tag. It may be present in 3.0.1 in the field, unmeasured: this host's load floor has never been attributed process by process.

Evidence kept in vc's scratchpad for this session: `intentd-31992-sample.txt`, `intentd-31992-evidence.txt` (the `ps -M` and `top` reads), `intentd-58837-cpu-trace.txt`. A watch is armed on the live daemon's CPU; on the next onset the capture is `sample` for five seconds, `lsof` for clients, and an lldb thread list with backtraces, so the hot thread is named by id rather than by order.

Remedy: none proposed until the hot site is named by a live capture. The CPU cost is one core for as long as it runs and nothing reports it; the daemon still answers throughout.

## Update, 2026-09-13, the replacement daemon

The replacement (pid 58837) reproduced it. It idled at 0.0% for five minutes, then went hot at 14:17:52Z (98.9%), forty seconds after vc's first `lldb -p` attach at 14:17:12Z; a second attach followed at 14:18:23Z. Both lldb runs were killed by a timeout and left their `debugserver` orphaned and attached. Killing both at 14:22:30Z did not stop it: 98.6% to 99.4% for the next minute, SYSBSD 89,996,496 by 14:23:42Z against 2:45 of CPU. The same thread by order (row 18, the store's serve thread) carried 1:20 system and 0:37 user at 99.4%. `sample` hangs on the hot process, traced or not, so no stacks this time. The duty cycle then dropped (59.8% at 14:24:14Z), as the first daemon's did.

So a debugger attach is one way to start it, and it sustains without the debugger. The first daemon's onset at about 14:05Z had no debugger; that trigger is still unknown. The capture that would name the hot thread by id with its CPU time is `sudo spindump <pid> 5 -file <path>`, which needs root and is hv's.

## Where the spin lives, from cc's reading of the pinned libraries (2026-09-13)

Both parks on the store thread, `rx.blocking_recv()` (store.rs:289) and `runtime.block_on(facade.graphql(..))` (store.rs:886), use tokio's one thread-local `CachedParkThread` (runtime/park.rs). Its `Inner::park` waits on a `parking_lot::Condvar` (the `parking_lot` feature is on through tokio's `full`), which reaches `parking_lot_core`'s `ThreadParker::park` on unix (thread_parker/unix.rs:73-82): lock its own pthread mutex, then `while should_park { pthread_cond_wait(..) }` with the return code checked only by a `debug_assert`, which a release build compiles out. `should_park` is cleared only by an unparker on another thread. So if `pthread_cond_wait` returns at once for any reason, the thread spins right there: one `__psynch_cvwait` per turn, never leaving `Inner::park`, nothing on any other thread. That is the sample's shape exactly, and it fits the numbers: a million syscalls a second on one thread with every other thread idle.

Apple's libpthread maps a `__psynch_cvwait` failure to EINTR (returned as 0), ETIMEDOUT, or EINVAL for everything else, and returns EINVAL up front on a bad mutex signature or a condvar busy with another mutex. A repeated EINTR fits the debugger trigger (suspending and resuming a thread interrupts the wait); a kernel-side error has precedent (graphia issue 33, `__psynch_cvwait` returning EBUSY on a thread that owned its mutex, macOS 10.15.7). The fault state is per thread: the pthread mutex and condvar live in that thread's `ThreadData`. A real send still gets through (the two `serve` samples), because it clears `should_park`; the next wait on the same condvar spins again. A restart makes a new thread.

Ruled out by the same reading: a waker outliving a GraphQL request (the schema is `Query, EmptyMutation, EmptySubscription` over a snapshot; the only async-graphql timer sites are websocket, multipart and dataloader, none used here), a stuck NOTIFIED (that spins in tokio's fast path with no condvar call), and a spurious-wake storm from another thread (no other thread shows CPU). Versions: tokio 1.53.1, parking_lot 0.12.5, parking_lot_core 0.9.12; neither changelog carries a fix on this path.

Not yet named: the errno. `sudo dtruss -t psynch_cvwait -p <pid>` on the hot daemon names it; a column of EINTR points at thread suspension, EINVAL or EBUSY at the kernel condvar state. Root, so hv's.

## dc's controls, 2026-09-13

- Run 1 (14:34Z): a fresh clone of e70c3528a, isolated HOME, delivered pair, the store built by a daemonless `st list`, the daemon started, one `graphql '{threads{id}}'` to open the project. It lit within a second of the open with no client after that, cooled, and burst again forty seconds later on its own. While hot the store's search tables did not move (index_file 1175 against file_index 1798, src_sections 187, unchanged across 14s at 99%). One thread, row 18 by `ps -M`, system over user, about 490k BSD syscalls a second.
- Run 2 (14:40Z to 14:50Z): the same clone and store after run 1's daemon had run on it, a fresh daemon, untouched for five minutes, then one open, then five minutes: cold throughout, 0.0% at every sample.

So the open alone is not the trigger and neither is the daemon alone. What differed is the store's state at open: freshly built, its index mid-reconcile. The live store's counts at 14:53Z were file_index 1800, index_file 1828, src_sections 778. Run 3 (the released 3.0.1 keg on a fresh clone) and run 4 (run 1's conditions again with the index counts read every ten seconds while hot) are the remaining measurements before a fix shape is ruled.
